items.text: The two pages declare different language codes: A uses a regional Australian English tag and B uses generic English
items.evidence: A lang="en-AU"; B lang="en"

items.text: A's h1 has no text. B's h1 holds the visible event name
items.evidence: A h1.text ""; B h1.text "LIQUI-MOLY BATHURST 12 HOUR"

items.text: B has a full heading hierarchy (h1, then an h2 'LATEST NEWS', then 7 h3 article titles, then h4s). A's outline contains only an empty h1 and one h4

items.text: Both sides wrap news items in 7 article elements, each with a time element

items.text: A's page title is 'Liqui-Moly Bathurst 12 Hour - Australia's International Endurance Race' with lang en-AU. B's is the shorter 'Liqui-Moly Bathurst 12 Hour' with lang en.
items.evidence: A title, lang 'en-AU'; B title, lang 'en'.

items.text: A's DOM is heavy and legacy-like: 48 scripts, 13 stylesheets, 4 style tags, 122 divs, 480 class usages across 174 unique classes, 10 inline style attributes. B is lean: 1 script, 0 stylesheets, 1 style tag, 21 divs, 49 classes (20 unique).
items.evidence: A counts scripts 48, stylesheets 13, div 122; B scripts 1, stylesheets 0, div 21, classes total 49.

items.text: B has two p elements, whereas A has no p tags. A's copy sits inside divs and spans.
items.evidence: B tag_counts p 2; A tag_counts has no p.

items.text: Page size differs. A is 3080px tall and B is 2511px, both 1440px wide. A has a large empty dark gap (~600px) between the news cards and the footer, while B's content flows continuously into the footer.
items.evidence: page_height A 3080 vs B 2511; A slice 1 empty space from y≈140–750.

items.text: A uses the -385x305 resized image variants (and a 770x480 featured one) at their original filenames. B uses differently named files, such as 'Bath12Hr-MH3.jpg', 'M20-fine.jpg' and 'MH1_2.jpg', for the same photos. B has the same natural sizes, but the filenames lack the size suffix.
items.evidence: A files 'M20_0362_fine-385x305.jpg'; B 'M20-fine.jpg'. Natural sizes 385x305 in both.

features.statement: Page declares a generic language code and a short, plain document title
The h1 contains the visible page/event name, with a complete heading hierarchy (h1, h2 section label, h3 item titles, h4s)
Icons are inline SVG rather than icon fonts
Typography uses only a system-ui font stack with no web fonts
Base body text is 16px with 24px line height
Subtitle is set in sentence/title case rather than all caps
Event dates appear in a solid red label box with white letter-spaced caps
Title is an oversized standalone hero block below the nav bar, above subtitle and dates
Navigation labels are short uppercase and wrap onto two lines when long
Featured story is split into an image on one side and a text panel on the other, not overlaid on the photo
Small badges and section labels are red, uppercase and letter-spaced
News is shown as a uniform multi-column card grid of equal-size cards with thin borders
Layout is built with CSS grid extensively
Each card includes a red uppercase 'READ MORE →' link with arrow
Dates are shown in muted grey secondary text
Featured item shows date and social share links
A single red accent color is used across labels, links and buttons
Dark near-black background with a slight blue tint and near-white body text
Small corner radii (about 6px) on buttons and cards, with no shadows, transforms or animations
Footer places small letter-spaced uppercase headings in side-by-side columns without decorative bars
Social icons are shown inside circular outlined buttons
Sponsor logos sit on white tiles in a dense multi-column grid
Menu toggle is a text button with padding and rounded corners
Markup is lean, with few scripts, no external stylesheets, few divs and few classes
Content flows continuously into the footer without large empty gaps, giving a shorter page
